     1	# stranger-monitor.yml — the package repo's scheduled stranger-door monitor (SPEC INV-148, INV-147).

     3	# manual dispatch for a verify hand-run), runs scripts/stranger-wish-monitor.py once, and pushes any inbox
     4	# file the monitor committed. Single instance by the concurrency group — a second scheduled run waits for
     5	# the in-flight one rather than racing its push (the CI form of the per-host lock the monitor keeps for a
     6	# host that runs the script directly, SPEC INV-147). It commits and pushes under the action's own token as

     8	# (SPEC M-6, INV-112). A GITHUB_TOKEN push does not re-trigger the gates workflow, which is correct for an
     9	# inbox deposit awaiting the next session's sweep.

    11	on:
    12	  schedule:
    13	    - cron: "17 6 * * *"   # daily at 06:17 UTC — an off-the-hour minute keeps clear of the top-of-hour crowd
    14	  workflow_dispatch:        # a manual hand-run, the verify path (SPEC INV-148 / M-290)

    16	# serialize runs: a second scheduled run waits for the in-flight one instead of cancelling it, so two runs
    17	# never overlap and race the push. cancel-in-progress stays false by intent (SPEC INV-148).
    18	concurrency:
    19	  group: stranger-monitor
    20	  cancel-in-progress: false
    21	
    22	permissions:
    23	  contents: write        # push the inbox commit the monitor makes
    24	  issues: write          # record the surfaced-generation marker comment on an Issue (SPEC INV-146)
    25	  discussions: write     # record it on a Discussion (SPEC INV-146)

    27	jobs:
    28	  monitor:
    29	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    30	    steps:
    31	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
    32	        with:
    33	          fetch-depth: 0    # the push step compares HEAD against origin to find the monitor's commit
    34	      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
    35	        with:
    36	          python-version: "3.12"
    37	      - name: identify the committer
    38	        run: |
    39	          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
    40	          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
    41	      - name: run the monitor
    42	        env:
    43	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}   # gh reads the token for `issue`/`api graphql`/`repo view`
    44	        run: python3 scripts/stranger-wish-monitor.py
    45	      - name: push any bridged inbox commit
    46	        run: |
    47	          # The monitor commits touching inbox/ only; push whatever it landed. A no-op run (no open
    48	          # stranger item) leaves nothing to push and exits clean. A rebase absorbs any commit main took
    49	          # since checkout, so the inbox commit lands without overwriting other work.
    50	          if [ -z "$(git log "origin/${GITHUB_REF_NAME}..HEAD" --oneline)" ]; then
    51	            echo "no bridged commit this run — nothing to push"
    52	            exit 0
    53	          fi
    54	          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
    55	            if git pull --rebase origin "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" && git push origin "HEAD:${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"; then
    56	              echo "pushed the bridged inbox commit"
    57	              exit 0
    58	            fi
    59	            echo "push attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying after rebase"
    60	          done
    61	          echo "could not push the bridged inbox commit after retries" >&2
    62	          exit 1

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# check-pin-drift.sh — gate (g): architecture pins must not rot (row 90, the
     3	# track-coach lesson: 7 of 17 pins drifted in ONE session, silently; row 541, the
     4	# 2026-08-05 prover pass that found 29 stale pins standing green under this gate;
     5	# row 588, where 48 of the r5 rule-price page's 53 range pins rotted unseen because
     6	# this gate read ARCHITECTURE.md alone — the r5 leg near the bottom of this file
     7	# closed that gap without touching the ARCHITECTURE.md check above it).
     8	#
     9	# A pin looks like `path/to/file:123` (label words) in a node section of
    10	# ARCHITECTURE.md, read through the one node reader guardrails/archformat.py
    11	# (--pins), never by slicing the node body here (SPEC INV-280). The NORMATIVE
    12	# pin is the named thing; the :line is a cache (SPEC E-14).
    13	#
    14	# THE MATCHING RULE (row 541, the prover record's own prescription in F4): a pin is
    15	# proved against its OWN line, by the words that NAME something.
    16	#   * A LINE pin (`file:N`, N > 1) — the label must be carried by line N itself,
    17	#     with a tolerance of ±2 lines, the width of one wrapped sentence and no more:
    18	#     one NAMING word of the label, four characters or more, must stand in that
    19	#     five-line window.
    20	#   * A NAMING word is any label word that is not document furniture. The furniture
    21	#     words — rule, step, gate, line, table, check, node, file, home, section, part,
    22	#     item, row, list, name, page, doc, entry — recur in every window of every
    23	#     rulebook, and matching on them is how the old gate read clean: a pin labelled
    24	#     "rule 20" sitting on rule 19's opening line matched the bare word "rule", and
    25	#     the 2026-08-05 pass found 29 stale pins that way. A furniture word counts only
    26	#     when the label carries no other word of four characters or more ("gates",
    27	#     "the rules"), so a label that names nothing else is still judged by what it has.
    28	#   * A FILE-LEVEL pin (`file:1`) names the file, not a line — line 1 of a script
    29	#     is a shebang and of a JSON file a brace — so its label is proved against the
    30	#     whole file, by the same naming words.
    31	#   * A pin carrying no label at all is proved by the file's existence, and the
    32	#     green line names those pins so the reader sees what went unproved.
    33	#
    34	# Every miss is named — the pin, the label, and what the target line actually
    35	# reads — and every miss is RED. The old gate reported a label miss as advisory
    36	# DRIFT unless --strict was passed, and the push chain passed no --strict, so the
    37	# 29 stale pins crossed a green gate. --strict is now the default; the flag is
    38	# still accepted so an installed host's wiring keeps working.
    39	#
    40	# RED — pinned file missing, :line beyond end of file, or the label not carried.
    41	#
    42	# Usage: check-pin-drift.sh [architecture-file] [--strict]
    43	
    44	set -euo pipefail
    45	
    46	# the one node reader sits beside this script (both in guardrails/), found by the script's own path so a
    47	# gate run against an ARCHITECTURE.md anywhere (a test fixture in a temp dir) still resolves the reader.
    48	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    49	ARCH="${1:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/ARCHITECTURE.md}"
    50	[ "${2:-}" = "--strict" ] && echo "note (pin drift): --strict is the default since row 541; the flag changes nothing."
    51	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$ARCH")" && pwd)"
    52	
    53	TOL=2            # the line-pin tolerance, in lines either side of the pinned line
    54	fail=0
    55	checked=0
    56	line_pins=0
    57	file_pins=0
    58	bare_pins=0
    59	bare_names=""
    60	read_files=""
    61	
    62	# Document furniture — the words every window of a rulebook holds. Singular forms; a
    63	# trailing "s" is stripped before the comparison.
    64	FURNITURE=" rule step gate line table check node file home section part item row list name page doc entry "
    65	
    66	# The label's words of four characters or more, whole and split at hyphens and
    67	# underscores, printed one per line: the naming words first, then the furniture
    68	# words, separated by a line reading `--`.
    69	label_words() {
    70	  local label="$1" w part naming="" furniture="" bare seen=" "
    71	  for w in $label; do
    72	    w="$(printf '%s' "$w" | tr -cd '[:alnum:]_-')"
    73	    for part in "$w" ${w//[-_]/ }; do
    74	      [ ${#part} -lt 4 ] && continue
    75	      bare="$(printf '%s' "$part" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    76	      case "$seen" in *" $bare "*) continue ;; esac
    77	      seen="$seen$bare "
    78	      bare="${bare%s}"
    79	      case "$FURNITURE" in
    80	        *" $bare "*) furniture="$furniture$part"$'\n' ;;
    81	        *)           naming="$naming$part"$'\n' ;;
    82	      esac
    83	    done
    84	  done
    85	  printf '%s--\n%s' "$naming" "$furniture"
    86	}
    87	
    88	# pins: `path:line` optionally followed by (label)
    89	while IFS=$'\t' read -r path line label; do
    90	  [ -z "$path" ] && continue
    91	  case "$path" in
    92	    "~/"*) full="$HOME/${path#\~/}" ;;
    93	    /*)    full="$path" ;;
    94	    *)     full="$ROOT/$path" ;;
    95	  esac
    96	  # A machine-local pin (~/ or absolute, outside the repo) exists only on the author's
    97	  # machine; in CI (the second net, SPEC M-5) it is noted and skipped, never a false red.
    98	  # It is skipped BEFORE the count, so the green line's arithmetic closes over the pins
    99	  # this run actually read; the note above names what stood outside it.
   100	  case "$path" in
   101	    "~/"*|/*)
   102	      if [ ! -f "$full" ] && [ "${CI:-}" = "true" ]; then
   103	        echo "note (pin drift): $path:$line — machine-local pin, absent in CI; skipped."
   104	        continue
   105	      fi ;;
   106	  esac
   107	  checked=$((checked+1))
   108	  if [ ! -f "$full" ]; then
   109	    echo "FAIL (pin drift): $path:$line — pinned file missing"; fail=1; continue
   110	  fi
   111	  read_files="$read_files$path"$'\n'
   112	  total=$(wc -l < "$full")
   113	  if [ "$line" -gt "$total" ]; then
   114	    echo "FAIL (pin drift): $path:$line — beyond end of file ($total lines)"; fail=1; continue
   115	  fi
   116	  if [ -z "$label" ]; then
   117	    bare_pins=$((bare_pins+1))
   118	    bare_names="$bare_names$path:$line, "
   119	    continue
   120	  fi
   121	
   122	  if [ "$line" -le 1 ]; then
   123	    file_pins=$((file_pins+1))
   124	    window="$(cat "$full")"
   125	    where="the file"
   126	  else
   127	    line_pins=$((line_pins+1))
   128	    lo=$(( line > TOL ? line - TOL : 1 ))
   129	    hi=$(( line + TOL ))
   130	    window="$(sed -n "${lo},${hi}p" "$full")"
   131	    where="lines $lo-$hi"
   132	  fi
   133	
   134	  # The words the pin is judged by: its naming words, or — when it has none — its
   135	  # furniture words. A hyphenated or underscored word is tried whole and in its parts,
   136	  # so `workshop-noise` matches "workshop noise" and `render_widget` its own halves.
   137	  words="$(label_words "$label")"
   138	  naming="$(awk 'BEGIN{before=1} /^--$/{before=0;next} before && NF' <<<"$words")"
   139	  if [ -n "$naming" ]; then
   140	    judged_by="$naming"
   141	    kind="naming word"
   142	  else
   143	    judged_by="$(awk 'BEGIN{after=0} /^--$/{after=1;next} after && NF' <<<"$words")"
   144	    kind="word"
   145	  fi
   146	
   147	  found=0
   148	  while IFS= read -r part; do
   149	    [ -z "$part" ] && continue
   150	    if grep -qiF -- "$part" <<<"$window"; then found=1; break; fi
   151	    if grep -qiF -- "${part%s}" <<<"$window"; then found=1; break; fi
   152	  done <<<"$judged_by"
   153	
   154	  if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
   155	    looked="$(printf '%s' "$judged_by" | paste -sd, - | sed 's/,/, /g')"
   156	    echo "FAIL (pin drift): $path:$line ($label) — no ${kind} of the label stands in $where; looked for [$looked]."
   157	    if [ "$line" -gt 1 ]; then
   158	      echo "    line $line reads: $(sed -n "${line}p" "$full" | cut -c1-100)"
   159	    fi
   160	    fail=1
   161	  fi
   162	done < <(python3 "$SCRIPT_DIR/archformat.py" --pins "$ARCH")
   163	
   164	if [ "$checked" -eq 0 ]; then
   165	  echo "FAIL (pin drift): no pins parsed from $ARCH"; exit 1
   166	fi
   167	
   168	if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
   169	  echo "  Fix: re-run the pin's grep and update the path/line, or re-label the pin to name what the line carries (SPEC E-14)."
   170	fi
   171	
   172	reach="$(printf '%s' "$read_files" | sed '/^$/d' | sort -u | paste -sd, - | sed 's/,/, /g')"
   173	# The word OK stands only over a leg that passed. The r5 leg below runs either way, so this
   174	# leg's verdict is decided here, before that leg can add findings of its own (row 588).
   175	arch_fail="$fail"
   176	if [ "$arch_fail" -eq 0 ]; then
   177	  echo "OK (pin drift): $checked pin(s) checked — $line_pins line pin(s) proved against their own line (tolerance ±$TOL lines), $file_pins file-level :1 pin(s) proved against the whole file, $bare_pins unlabelled pin(s) proved by the file's existence alone: ${bare_names%, }."
   178	else
   179	  echo "FAILED (pin drift): $checked pin(s) checked in $(basename "$ARCH"), and the findings above stand."
   180	fi
   181	echo "  reach: files=[$(basename "$ARCH"), $reach]"
   182	
   183	# --- the .live-spec range-pin leg (ROADMAP row 588) ---------------------------------------
   184	# ARCHITECTURE.md is not the only page that pins a line — the r5 rule-price page pins 53 skill
   185	# rules by `path:start-end`, a RANGE rather than a single line, and it rotted unseen because

+"""gen-tree-counts.py — build every count this repository publishes about its own tree from the tree.

+repository, and fills the generated block on every page that carries one. A page keeping its own
+hand-written sentence is left alone here: the gate `guardrails/check-tree-counts.py` renders that
+sentence from the same measurement and reds where the page does not carry it.

+stage a list of literal argument tokens. Two things come out of that one field: what runs, and what a
+reader is shown. What runs is `subprocess.Popen` with `shell=False`, stages wired to each other by
+pipes, so no shell is involved at any point and a token holding a semicolon, a backtick, a redirect or
+a dollar sign is an ordinary argument with no power. What a reader is shown is `render_command`, which
+prints the same list. The reader's copy and the run therefore cannot drift, because they are one
+field. An edit to an `argv` changes what a push measures, so the registry is reviewed the way a change
+to a check script is reviewed (SPEC R306, INV-305).

+    programs that read and none that writes. A stage naming anything else reds, and no stage of that
+    command runs.
